segments: Page 88. Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
Kingdom.
Now Sophia, when she heard, was afraid,
and she commanded, and the wife of Tiberius came and entered in pomp.
And by the crowds she was named Helena,
as if in praise. Now Tiberius greatly honored Sophia and her daughter,
and increased their revenues,
and took up residence within their palace.
Also Mundhir bar Harith, when he heard that Tiberius had become emperor, went up to Constantinople.
And when the emperor accused him of neglecting the aid of the Romans,
he showed him Justin's letter.
And when Tiberius saw it, he was astonished,
and he greatly honored Mundhir,
and gave him lavish gifts, and he departed.
And after these things, Maurice, Caesar of the Romans, went up to the emperor Tiberius and slandered Mundhir.
And a certain Magnus, a Syrian military commander, promised to capture him,
because he was his friend.
And when he went out to Syria,
he sent to Mundhir, saying:
"I desire that you come to me so that I may see your health,
inasmuch as I am very exhausted from the toil of the journey;
otherwise, I myself would have come to greet you."
And when he trusted him as a friend,
and came,
he bound him,
and sent him to the royal city.
Then Naaman his son gathered armies,
and began plundering the lands of the Romans.
However, he did not commit murder or burning,
on account of his father, who was imprisoned.
Then the accursed Magnus wished to deceive this one as well,
and sent to him with oaths, saying: "If you come to me,
I will establish you in your father's place."
And he brought one of the youths and dressed him in his garments,
and sent him with servants.
Now Magnus, when he saw him, said to him:
"Are you Naaman?" And he said:
"It is I;
behold, I have come according to your command."
Then he ordered:
"Behold the rebel against the emperor!
Put irons on him!"
Then that one laughed and said:
"No, by Christ,
I am not Naaman!"
And when Magnus sought to torture the youth,
the Arab said:
"I do not care,
for if I had not come,
I would have been killed by my king."
And on this account, after tortures, he dismissed {OCR?} him.
And after a little while, Magnus died.
Then Naaman, having despaired of his life, went up to Maurice,
the emperor.
It is an injustice, therefore, with which the Jacobites wrong the members of the Catholic Church
